verification_note: A prior session in this build directory left only a live_readme.md file with no other evidence -- that file was treated as stale/unverified per instruction and re-fetched fresh here (new source_revision/readme_blob_sha recorded above; both GitHub API reads were re-run in this session). No C++ compiler/CMake toolchain is available on this machine, so source-level verification is code-reading only via the GitHub Contents API and GitHub code search. However, the README's Installation section makes specific, falsifiable claims about the *published NuGet package's own contents* (not just the repository source) -- this session downloaded the real, currently-published aspose.cells.cpp.foss.26.4.1.nupkg from api.nuget.org (a real artifact, not fabricated) and inspected its contents directly with Python's zipfile module (no execution of any code from the package, only archive-listing and text extraction), which is real verification against the actual published artifact, not just the repository source tree -- notably, this repository's own git history contains no NuGet-packaging files (.nuspec, .targets, lib/win_x86 binaries) at all, so this cross-check against the live NuGet artifact was necessary to confirm the Installation section's claims could not be verified from source alone.

facts.claim: Aspose.Cells FOSS for C++ is published on NuGet as Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS, version 26.4.1
facts.evidence: GET https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/aspose.cells.cpp.foss/index.json -> {"versions": ["26.4.0", "26.4.1"]}, HTTP 200. Downloaded aspose.cells.cpp.foss.26.4.1.nupkg directly (25,536,573 bytes) and read its Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS.nuspec: <id>Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS</id><version>26.4.1</version> -- exact match.

facts.claim: The package ships prebuilt static libraries for Windows only (lib/win_x86, lib/win_x86_64) built with the MSVC v14x toolset; its own bundled aspose.cells.cpp.foss.targets file errors the build for any other toolset or platform. There are no Linux/macOS binaries in the package.
facts.evidence: Listed all 201 entries in the downloaded nupkg (a zip archive) directly: the only .lib files present are build/native/Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS/lib/win_x86/{Debug,Release}/aspose_cells_foss.lib and lib/win_x86_64/{Debug,Release}/aspose_cells_foss.lib -- no linux/macos/arm/.a/.so/.dylib entries anywhere in the archive. Read build/native/Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS/aspose.cells.cpp.foss.targets directly from the nupkg: its PlatformCheck MSBuild target contains `<Error Condition="!$(PlatformToolset.Contains('v14'))" Text="Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS Library error: Only 'v14x' toolset is supported." />` and `<Error Condition="'$(Platform)' != 'x64' And '$(Platform)' != 'Win32'" Text="...Only 'x64' and 'Win32' platforms are supported..." />` -- exact match to the README's claim, down to the quoted toolset name.

facts.claim: A CMake project on Windows can point at the package's own bundled config, which defines an Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS imported target
facts.evidence: Confirmed build/native/Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS/aspose.cells.cpp.foss-config.cmake exists in the downloaded nupkg's file listing, at the exact path the README's CMake snippet references (build/native/Aspose.Cells.Cpp.FOSS).

facts.claim: LoadFormat and SaveFormat each declare a single Xlsx member
facts.evidence: Read Aspose.Cells.Foss.Cpp/include/aspose/cells_foss/LoadFormat.h directly: `enum class LoadFormat { Auto = 0, Xlsx = 1 };` -- LoadFormat declares TWO members (Auto and Xlsx), not a single Xlsx member. SaveFormat.h does declare exactly one member (`enum class SaveFormat { Xlsx = 0 };`), so the claim is accurate for SaveFormat but factually wrong for LoadFormat.

facts.claim: saving to any other format throws UnsupportedFeatureException("Only XLSX save is supported.")
facts.evidence: Read Aspose.Cells.Foss.Cpp/src/aspose/cells_foss/XlsxWorkbookSerializer.cpp directly, line 738-739: `if (options.GetSaveFormat() != SaveFormat::Xlsx) { throw UnsupportedFeatureException("Only XLSX save is supported."); }` -- exact message match. (Given SaveFormat's single-member enum, this branch is effectively unreachable through normal public API use, but the code and message exist exactly as claimed.)

facts.claim: Legacy SpreadsheetML mapper classes (WorkbookXmlMapper, WorksheetXmlMapper, StylesheetXmlMapper, SharedStringTableXmlMapper) exist in source but their read/write methods unconditionally throw UnsupportedFeatureException
facts.evidence: GitHub code search confirmed UnsupportedFeatureException is referenced in all four files (WorkbookXmlMapper.cpp, WorksheetXmlMapper.cpp, StylesheetXmlMapper.cpp, SharedStringTableXmlMapper.cpp). Read WorkbookXmlMapper.cpp directly: both its methods unconditionally `throw UnsupportedFeatureException(...)` with no implementation body.

facts.claim: Cell-level comments/notes are not modeled as a distinct object. The only Comment field in the public API belongs to DefinedName — a description string on a named range, not an Excel cell note or threaded comment.
facts.evidence: Read DefinedName.h directly: confirms GetComment()/SetComment() exist there, matching half the claim. However, a GitHub code search for 'Comment' under the include/ directory also found DocumentProperties.h, which defines a second, distinct Comment-named field: `GetComments()`/`SetComments()`, mapped to the OOXML core.xml 'Description' property via `_model.GetCore().SetDescription(...)`. This is document-level metadata, not a cell note either, so the underlying substance of the bullet (no Excel cell-level comment/note object exists) is not falsified -- but the specific, falsifiable phrase 'The only Comment field in the public API belongs to DefinedName' is literally false: DocumentProperties::Comments is a second one.

facts.claim: An unsupported [conditional formatting] rule type is dropped with a WarningInfo diagnostic rather than failing the load outright
facts.evidence: Read Aspose.Cells.Foss.Cpp/src/aspose/cells_foss/XlsxWorkbookConditionalFormatting.cpp directly, line 419: constructs a WarningInfo with the message "An unsupported conditional formatting rule was dropped during load." -- confirms the claim precisely.
